name: @programcomputer/nasa-mcp-server

tools.name: nasa_apod
tools.description: NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) from the NASA Science APOD API (science.nasa.gov): the latest picture, one date (1995-06-16 onward), or a date range of up to 100 days. Returns the title, credit, explanation as plain text, image or video URL and page link, and embeds up to max_images pictures. No API key needed.

date.description: Date of the picture (YYYY-MM-DD, 1995-06-16 or later). Defaults to the latest published picture. Cannot be combined with start_date/end_date.

end_date.description: End of a date range (YYYY-MM-DD); requires start_date. Defaults to today (UTC) when start_date is given.

max_images.description: How many pictures to embed as image content (0-5). Remaining entries are listed by URL.

annotations.title: NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day

tools.name: nasa_neo
tools.description: Near-Earth asteroid close approaches from NASA NeoWs: a feed for up to 7 days (defaults to today, UTC) or a single asteroid by ID. Requires NASA_API_KEY.

start_date.description: Start date for the close-approach feed (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to today (UTC).

end_date.description: End date (YYYY-MM-DD), at most 7 days after start_date. Defaults to start_date.

asteroid_id.description: Look up one asteroid by its NeoWs ID instead of the date feed.

annotations.title: NASA Near Earth Object Web Service

tools.name: nasa_epic
tools.description: Earth Polychromatic Imaging Camera (DSCOVR) full-disc Earth images for a day: metadata for every image plus a bounded number embedded.

date.description: Date of the images (YYYY-MM-DD). Defaults to the most recent available day.

max_images.description: How many images to embed (0-3, JPEG). All images are listed with PNG and JPEG URLs.

tools.name: nasa_gibs
tools.description: Render a Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS) layer for a date and bounding box as an image (WMS GetMap, EPSG:4326).

resolution.description: Output resolution in pixels per degree (default 2, i.e. 720x360 for the whole globe).

bbox.description: Area as west,south,east,north in decimal degrees (EPSG:4326). Defaults to the whole globe.

tools.name: nasa_cmr
tools.description: Search NASA's Common Metadata Repository (CMR) for Earth science collections (datasets) or granules (files). Supports identifiers, temporal and spatial filters (bounding_box, point, polygon, line, circle), platform/instrument/project, facets and sorting. Returns a compact normalized envelope by default (response_mode raw for upstream metadata) and a next_cursor for Search After pagination: continue by passing only {"cursor": next_cursor}. Collection matches describe datasets; they do not prove granules exist for a given time or place. No API key needed.

format.description: Upstream CMR metadata format. json/umm_json support compact output; others are returned raw. dif, dif10, opendata: collections only; stac: granules only.

response_mode.description: compact (default for json/umm_json): normalized records. raw: upstream metadata as returned (default for other formats).

fields.description: Compact mode only: normalized fields to return. concept_id is always included. Defaults to all fields except summary.

cursor.description: next_cursor from a previous response. Continue with the cursor alone; omitted filters are restored from it.

page.description: DEPRECATED page-number pagination (CMR page_num). Prefer cursor. Cannot be combined with cursor or offset.

offset.description: DEPRECATED offset pagination. Prefer cursor. Cannot be combined with cursor or page.

concept_id.description: Concept ID(s). For granule searches a collection concept ID (C...) also selects that collection, as in CMR.

collection_concept_id.description: Granules only: collection concept ID(s) to search within.

readable_granule_name.description: Granules only: granule name (supports CMR * and ? wildcards).

temporal.description: Temporal range "start,end" in ISO 8601 (date or date-time, UTC assumed). Either side may be empty, e.g. "2020-01-01T00:00:00Z,".

bounding_box.description: Bounding box west,south,east,north (lon/lat degrees). west > east crosses the antimeridian (supported by CMR).

bbox.description: Compatibility alias for bounding_box (sent to CMR as bounding_box).

polygon.description: Polygon "lon1,lat1,...,lon1,lat1": closed, counter-clockwise (CMR rejects clockwise rings).

processing_level_id.description: Collections only: processing level(s), e.g. 3, L2.

granule_data_format.description: Collections only: granule data format(s), e.g. netCDF-4.

cloud_cover.description: Granules only: cloud cover range "min,max" in percent.

day_night_flag.description: Granules only: DAY, NIGHT, BOTH or UNSPECIFIED.

has_granules.description: Collections only: require (true) or exclude (false) collections with granules.

cloud_hosted.description: Collections only: restrict to cloud-hosted (true) or not (false).

downloadable.description: Only records with (true) or without (false) downloadable data links.

browsable.description: Only records with (true) or without (false) browse imagery.

include_facets.description: Include CMR v2 facets (counts by keyword, platform, ...).

sort_key.description: Sort key(s), "-" prefix for descending. Collections: score, usage_score, entry_title, dataset_id, short_name, entry_id, start_date, end_date, platform, instrument, sensor, provider, revision_date, has_granules, create-data-date, ongoing. Granules: start_date, end_date, producer_granule_id, readable_granule_name, granule_ur, revision_date, cloud_cover, day_night_flag, data_size, provider, platform, instrument, sensor, online_only, browsable, entry_title, short_name, version, campaign, project.

tools.name: nasa_firms
tools.description: Active fire/thermal anomaly detections from NASA FIRMS for a bounding box and 1-5 day window. Requires FIRMS_MAP_KEY (not NASA_API_KEY). The legacy latitude/longitude interface now needs radius_km and is converted to a bbox.

bbox.description: Area as west,south,east,north in decimal degrees (preferred). Antimeridian-crossing boxes are rejected.

latitude.description: Legacy area center latitude; requires longitude and radius_km.

longitude.description: Legacy area center longitude; requires latitude and radius_km.

radius_km.description: Half-width in kilometres of the box built around latitude/longitude (converted to a bbox before querying).

days.description: DAY_RANGE: number of days of detections (1-5).

date.description: First day of the window (YYYY-MM-DD); FIRMS returns [date, date + days - 1]. Omit for the most recent data.

source.description: FIRMS sensor/product. *_NRT is near real-time, *_SP is standard processing.

limit.description: Maximum detections returned (1-2000). total_detections reports the full count.

tools.name: nasa_images
tools.description: Search NASA's Image and Video Library. Returns item metadata and URLs, with a bounded number of preview thumbnails embedded.

max_images.description: How many preview thumbnails to embed (0-5). Every item is listed with its URLs.

annotations.title: NASA Image and Video Library search

tools.name: nasa_exoplanet
tools.description: Query the NASA Exoplanet Archive through its TAP service (ADQL). Tables use current TAP names such as ps, pscomppars, cumulative and toi.

table.description: TAP table, e.g. ps (Planetary Systems), pscomppars, cumulative (Kepler KOI), toi.

select.description: Columns to return (ADQL select list). Defaults to *.

where.description: ADQL WHERE condition, e.g. disc_year > 2020 and discoverymethod = 'Transit'.

order.description: ADQL ORDER BY expression, e.g. pl_name.

tools.name: nasa_donki
tools.description: Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information (DONKI) events by type for up to 30 days at a time, from the NASA CCMC DONKI API (ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov): solar flares, CMEs and their analyses, geomagnetic storms, interplanetary shocks, SEP, MPC, RBE and HSS events, WSA-ENLIL simulations and notifications. Compact one-line summaries by default; response_mode raw returns the full records. No API key needed.

type.description: Event type: cme, cmea, gst, ips, flr, sep, mpc, rbe, hss, wsa, notifications.

startDate.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD). With only endDate, 30 days before endDate; with neither, the last 30 days.

endDate.description: End date (YYYY-MM-DD), at most 30 days after startDate. Defaults to today.

response_mode.description: compact (default): one line per event with its key fields. raw: the full DONKI records as JSON (large for cme, cmea and wsa).

limit.description: Return only the most recent N events. Applied by this server; DONKI has no limit parameter.

tools.name: nasa_mars_rover
tools.description: DEPRECATED: the upstream Mars Rover Photos API (api.nasa.gov/mars-photos) has been returning HTTP 404 "No such app" since at least 2026-09-29. Calls still query it and report the upstream status accurately; no photos are fabricated. Requires NASA_API_KEY.

sol.description: Martian sol of the photos. Provide sol or earth_date.

earth_date.description: Earth date of the photos (YYYY-MM-DD). Provide sol or earth_date.

tools.name: nasa_eonet
tools.description: Natural events (wildfires, storms, volcanoes, ice, ...) from the Earth Observatory Natural Event Tracker. Filters are sent exactly as given; no automatic broadening.

category.description: EONET category ID(s), comma-separated: e.g. wildfires, severeStorms, volcanoes, seaLakeIce.

days.description: Only events active within this many prior days.

source.description: EONET source ID(s), comma-separated, e.g. InciWeb,EO.

tools.name: nasa_power
tools.description: Daily solar and meteorological data for a point from NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources).

community.description: User community: RE (renewable energy), SB (sustainable buildings), AG (agroclimatology).

time_standard.description: Time standard for daily values; POWER defaults to LST (local solar time) when omitted.

tools.name: nasa_osdr_files
tools.description: List the data files (with download links) for a NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) study.

accession_number.description: OSD study accession number, e.g. 87 or OSD-87.

tools.name: nasa_insight_weather
tools.description: HISTORICAL DATA ONLY: per-sol Mars surface weather (air temperature, pressure, wind) from NASA's InSight lander at Elysium Planitia. The feed is frozen at the last seven sols it reported (sols 675-681, October 2020) and is no longer updated. Requires NASA_API_KEY.

tools.name: nasa_tle
tools.description: Two-line element sets (TLE) for Earth-orbiting satellites from the TLE API in the api.nasa.gov catalog (tle.ivanstanojevic.me; CelesTrak data refreshed daily): one satellite by NORAD catalog number, or a paged name search. No API key needed.

satellite_id.description: NORAD catalog number, e.g. 25544 for the ISS. Cannot be combined with search options.

search.description: Search satellite names, e.g. "ISS" or "HUBBLE". Omit to browse all records.

sort.description: Sort field for searches (upstream default popularity).

tools.name: nasa_ssc_observatories
tools.description: Spacecraft and other observatories whose locations the NASA Satellite Situation Center (SSCWeb) can compute, with their data time ranges and resolution. Use the IDs with nasa_ssc_locations. No API key needed.

search.description: Case-insensitive text to match in the observatory ID or name, e.g. "mms" or "GOES".

active_on.description: Only observatories with location data on this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

tools.name: nasa_ssc_locations
tools.description: Positions of spacecraft (and the Moon and Sun) over a time range from the NASA Satellite Situation Center (SSCWeb), in geophysical coordinate systems (GEO, GM, GSE, GSM, SM, GEI). Returns a CSV table per observatory: X/Y/Z in km, latitude/longitude in degrees, local time in hours and radial distance in km. The resolution factor is raised automatically to keep the output bounded. No API key needed.

observatories.description: 1-5 SSC observatory IDs, e.g. ["iss"] or ["mms1", "moon"] (see nasa_ssc_observatories). A comma-separated string also works.

start_time.description: Start time (UTC), e.g. 2026-09-29T06:00:00Z; a bare date such as 2026-09-29 means 00:00 UTC.

end_time.description: End time (UTC); at most 366 days after start_time.

coordinate_systems.description: Coordinate systems (default geo): geo, gm, gse, gsm, sm, geitod, geij2000. A comma-separated string also works.

resolution_factor.description: Return every Nth point of each observatory's base resolution (60-720 s). Chosen automatically when omitted to keep the output bounded.

tools.name: nasa_techport
tools.description: NASA's technology project inventory (TechPort): search projects by keyword, or fetch one project with its status, dates, program, technology readiness levels (TRL), lead organization, description and benefits. No API key needed.

query.description: Search TechPort technology projects, e.g. "solar sail". Results are ordered by relevance.

project_id.description: Fetch one project by its TechPort ID, e.g. 94703.

limit.description: Search mode: how many projects to return (1-50, default 10).

tools.name: nasa_techtransfer
tools.description: Search NASA's Technology Transfer portfolio (technology.nasa.gov): patents available for licensing, issued patents, the NASA Software Catalog, or Spinoff stories about commercial products that use NASA technology. No API key needed.

query.description: Keywords to search for, e.g. "engine" or "solar panel".

collection.description: What to search: patent (licensable patents), patent_issued, software (NASA Software Catalog) or spinoff (Spinoff stories).

limit.description: How many results to return (1-50). The service returns every match; the rest are counted but not shown.

tools.name: nasa_trek_layers
tools.description: Search the map layer catalogs of NASA Mars Trek, Moon Trek and Vesta Trek (trek.nasa.gov): mosaics, colour hillshades and other imagery served as OGC WMTS tiles. Returns layer IDs for nasa_trek_tile, with mission, instrument and WMTS endpoint. No API key needed.

projection.description: Map projection: equirectangular (global), north_pole or south_pole (polar stereographic).

search.description: Keywords to match, e.g. "olympus", "LRO WAC" or "HiRISE".

annotations.title: NASA Trek map layers (Mars, Moon, Vesta)

tools.name: nasa_trek_tile
tools.description: One WMTS map tile image from NASA Mars Trek, Moon Trek or Vesta Trek for a layer from nasa_trek_layers, addressed by zoom/row/col or (equirectangular layers) by latitude/longitude. Reads the layer's WMTS capabilities to validate the tile and pick the format. No API key needed.

layer.description: Layer ID from nasa_trek_layers, e.g. Mars_MGS_MOLA_ClrShade_merge_global_463m or LRO_WAC_Mosaic_Global_303ppd_v02.

projection.description: Map projection: equirectangular (global), north_pole or south_pole (polar stereographic).

zoom.description: Zoom level (WMTS TileMatrix). 0 is the whole layer; each level doubles the resolution.

row.description: Tile row (0 at the top). Provide row and col, or latitude and longitude.

latitude.description: Equirectangular only: pick the tile containing this latitude (degrees).

longitude.description: Equirectangular only: pick the tile containing this longitude (degrees east, -180 to 360).

annotations.title: NASA Trek map tile (Mars, Moon, Vesta)

tools.name: nasa_mast_observations
tools.description: Search the Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes (MAST), NASA's archive for TESS, Hubble, JWST, Kepler/K2 and other missions, for observations of a named object, a TIC ID or a sky position. For TESS (the default) it lists light curves of the matching TIC stars with their sectors: SPOC 2-minute and 20-second light curves and high-level science product (HLSP) light curves such as QLP and TESS-SPOC, made from full-frame images. Other collections and data product types use MAST's position search, which can take a minute when MAST is busy. Returns obsid values for nasa_mast_products (files and download links). No API key needed.

target.description: Object name resolved by MAST (SIMBAD, NED or the TESS Input Catalog), e.g. "Pi Mensae", "TRAPPIST-1", "M31" or "TIC 261136679".

ra.description: Right ascension in decimal degrees (ICRS). Use with dec instead of target or tic_id.

dec.description: Declination in decimal degrees (ICRS). Use with ra.

radius_arcsec.description: Search radius in arcseconds (max 600). TESS light curve searches match TIC stars within it (default 10). Other searches match observations whose footprint overlaps the circle (default 60, because recent observations of fast-moving nearby stars such as TRAPPIST-1 lie tens of arcseconds from their catalog position).

collection.description: MAST collection (mission), e.g. TESS, HST, JWST, Kepler, K2, GALEX, SWIFT, PS1 or HLSP (high-level science products). "all" searches every collection. TESS light curve searches also include TESS high-level science products such as QLP and TESS-SPOC.

dataproduct_type.description: Only this data product type. For TESS, light curves (timeseries) are listed by default; image lists full-frame image observations, which nasa_tess_ffi covers faster.

limit.description: How many observations to list, newest first (1-200). Counts in the summary cover all matches.

annotations.title: MAST observations (TESS, Hubble, JWST, Kepler and more)

tools.name: nasa_mast_products
tools.description: List the files of MAST observations (from nasa_mast_observations), such as TESS light curves and target pixel files or Hubble and JWST images and spectra, with type, size and a download URL for each. Files are not downloaded or embedded. No API key needed.

obsids.description: 1-20 numeric obsid values from nasa_mast_observations (not the obs_id text). A comma-separated string also works.

product_types.description: Product types to list (default science): science, info (for example TESS data validation reports), preview and auxiliary.

subgroups.description: Only these product subgroups, e.g. ["LC"] for TESS light curves, ["TP"] for target pixel files, ["DRZ", "FLT"] for Hubble images or ["X1D"] for spectra. High-level science products (HLSP) have no subgroup, so this filter leaves them out.

minimum_recommended.description: Only MAST's minimum recommended products (useful for Hubble and JWST, which list many intermediate files).

annotations.title: MAST data products and download links

tools.name: nasa_tess_ffi
tools.description: Which TESS sectors, cameras and CCDs observed a sky position in their full-frame images (FFIs), with sector dates and a TESSCut download URL for a cutout of each sector (a ZIP of FITS target pixel files made from SPOC FFIs). Works for any star, including those without 2-minute light curves. Accepts an object name, TIC ID or coordinates. Cutouts are not downloaded. No API key needed.

target.description: Object name resolved by MAST (SIMBAD, NED or the TESS Input Catalog), e.g. "Pi Mensae", "TRAPPIST-1", "M31" or "TIC 261136679".

ra.description: Right ascension in decimal degrees (ICRS). Use with dec instead of target or tic_id.

dec.description: Declination in decimal degrees (ICRS). Use with ra.

cutout_size.description: Width and height of each cutout in TESS pixels (21″ each), 1-100. TESSCut limits a cutout to 10,000 pixels.

annotations.title: TESS full-frame image sectors and cutouts (TESSCut)

tools.name: jpl_sbdb
tools.description: Orbital and physical data for one asteroid or comet from the JPL Small-Body Database (SBDB).

sstr.description: Search string: name, designation or number (e.g. Ceres, 433, 2019 OK).

ca_body.description: Limit close approaches to this body (e.g. Earth); needs ca_data.

tools.name: jpl_fireball
tools.description: Fireball (bolide) events reported by US Government sensors, from the JPL Fireball API.

tools.name: jpl_jd_cal
tools.description: Convert between Julian dates and calendar dates (UTC) with the JPL JD-Calendar API.

jd.description: Julian date to convert to a calendar date.

cd.description: Calendar date (UTC) to convert to a Julian date.

tools.name: jpl_nhats
tools.description: Near-Earth objects accessible to human missions (NHATS): a constrained summary list, or one object by des/spk.

dur.description: Maximum total mission duration in days (60-450).

stay.description: Minimum stay at the NEO in days (8, 16, 24 or 32).

plot.description: Include a base64 plot (object mode; large).

tools.name: jpl_cad
tools.description: Asteroid and comet close approaches to the planets, past and future, from the JPL SBDB Close-Approach Data API.

dist_max.description: Maximum approach distance, e.g. 0.05 (au) or 10LD. Default 0.05 au.

date_min.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD, now, or +/-days). Default now.

body.description: Close-approach body (Earth, Mars, ALL, ...). Default Earth.

sort.description: Sort field, prefix - for descending. Default date.

tools.name: jpl_sentry
tools.description: Earth impact risk assessments from JPL Sentry: summary table, one object, virtual impactors, or removed objects.

des.description: Object mode: designation, e.g. 29075 or 2011 AG5.

h_max.description: Summary/VI mode: maximum absolute magnitude H.

ps_min.description: Summary/VI mode: minimum Palermo Scale value, e.g. -3.

ip_min.description: Summary/VI mode: minimum impact probability, e.g. 1e-5.

all.description: Virtual-impactor mode: all VIs (combine with ip_min/ps_min/h_max to narrow).

limit.description: Return at most this many records from list modes. Applied by this server: Sentry has no limit parameter.

tools.name: jpl_horizons
tools.description: Ephemerides and object data for solar-system bodies from the JPL Horizons API (GET).

tools.name: jpl_horizons_file
tools.description: Same as jpl_horizons, but submits the parameters as a Horizons input file (POST to horizons_file.api).

tools.name: jpl_periodic_orbits
tools.description: Periodic orbits (halo, DRO, Lyapunov, ...) in three-body systems from the JPL Three-Body Periodic Orbits database.

sys.description: Three-body system, e.g. earth-moon, sun-earth, mars-phobos.

family.description: Orbit family, e.g. halo, dro, lyapunov, vertical, axial, butterfly.

branch.description: Branch (required by some families), e.g. N or S.

tools.name: jpl_scout
tools.description: JPL Scout trajectory analysis and hazard assessment for unconfirmed objects on the Minor Planet Center NEO Confirmation Page.

plot.description: Object mode: base64 plots to include: el (elements), ca (close approach), sr (systematic ranging), colon-separated.

file.description: Object mode: include the observation file as a list or in MPC format.

n_orbits.description: Object mode: number of sampled orbits (1-1000).

limit.description: List mode: return at most this many objects. Applied by this server; Scout has no limit parameter.

tools.name: jpl_mission_design
tools.description: Ballistic mission options to asteroids and comets from the JPL Small-Body Mission Design API. Object mode (des, spk or sstr) returns the pre-computed mission options stored for one object (launch and arrival dates, V-infinity, time of flight). List mode returns the most accessible small bodies for the given launch years, ranked by crit, with optional SBDB filters. Porkchop-plot maps (mode M) and mission-extension searches (mode T) are not exposed.

des.description: Object mode: designation, e.g. 2012 TC4 or 433.

sstr.description: Object mode: search string (name, designation or SPK-ID), e.g. apophis.

class.description: Object mode: orbit class as a name instead of the three-letter code.

crit.description: List mode: optimality criterion. 1 min departure V-infinity (default), 2 min arrival V-infinity, 3 min total delta-V, 4-6 the same with minimum time of flight first.

year.description: List mode: launch year(s), from the current year up to 20 years ahead. JPL defaults to the next five years.

lim.description: List mode: how many accessible objects to return (1-200).

sb_kind.description: List mode: asteroids (a) or comets (c) only.

sb_group.description: List mode: NEOs or PHAs only.

sb_class.description: List mode: orbit class code(s), e.g. APO or MBA,OMB (case-sensitive).

sb_ns.description: List mode: numbered (n) or unnumbered (u) objects only.

sb_sat.description: List mode: only objects with at least one known satellite.

instructions: Read-only access to public NASA and JPL APIs. nasa_cmr returns a compact envelope with next_cursor; continue a search by passing only the cursor.
